summary.headline: Snowman guides 10-15% top-line growth for FY27 despite war-driven volume dip; Gateway ICD volumes stagnant, DFC-JNPT link now complete.
summary.overview: Joint Gateway Distriparks and Snowman Logistics call covering Q1 FY27. Management attributed the volume softness to the West Asia conflict (since April), which cut imports sharply in April-May, and to July weather disruptions at ports; market share is described as intact while the underlying market has de-grown. Snowman pricing rose 5-7% on average across warehousing customers, and management guided 10-15% top-line growth across all segments. Rail EBITDA was pressured by lower double-stacking (39% vs 40-42% earlier), higher underframe and empty running, and wage and fuel inflation, with relief expected from Q2. Management reported no specific Q1 financial figures in the call.

segments.name: Gateway ICD / rail
segments.commentary: Market share intact but market de-grew in operating regions; JNPT exposure about 5% of rail volume. Rail EBITDA per TEU fell on lower double-stacking, higher empty running and underframe usage, and wage and fuel costs.

segments.name: Snowman warehousing
segments.commentary: Pricing up 5-7% on average; about 24,000 additional pallets expected by end of FY27 (Pune first, then Patna).

segments.name: Snowman 5PL
segments.commentary: Service margin typically 5-6%; no new 5PL customer added in Q1, with new names possibly by Q3-Q4.

segments.name: CFS (Gateway)
segments.commentary: Volumes improved and a pricing increase taken to offset fuel and wage hikes; margin uplift possible in Q2. Management is not actively pursuing a sale.

segments.name: Domestic transport (Snowman)
segments.commentary: Around 500 containers a month currently, with scope to scale as network expands.

guidance_outlook: Gateway expects to close FY27 with double-digit volume growth, conditional on the West Asia situation easing.
Snowman guided 10-15% top-line growth for the year, across all segments.
Ankleshwar ICD to start EXIM operations by end of September 2026 (Q2); current volume zero.
Indore ICD operational by 2028; Jaipur ICD still awaiting final arguments in September 2026.
Rail EBITDA and margin expected to recover as volumes return and fuel and wage cost pass-throughs flow through in Q2.
capex_capacity: Indore ICD land expanded to about 26.4 acres; construction slowed by rains, expected to reach full swing after September 2026.
Snowman adding about 24,000 pallets by end of FY27, with Pune commissioning in a couple of months and Patna to follow; similar additions planned in subsequent years.
Gateway land bank about 475 acres across India, mostly freehold; Garhi land (85-90 acres) indicated at INR 25-30 crore per acre on outright purchase basis.
Ankleshwar is expected to be a new EXIM location, currently served by one ICD estimated at about 5,000 TEU, with a 3-4 year ramp to a similar scale.
demand_pricing: West Asia conflict since April cut imports sharply in April-May; imports improved from June-July, but July volumes were hit by weather-related port and double-stacking restrictions at Mundra and JNPT.
Management said June and July trends were similar to Q1 and declined to give specific monthly figures, citing listed-company restrictions.
Shipping lines reportedly prefer single-dip over double-dip on the West Coast, which could shift some volume to JNPT; management described this as early, exploratory.
JNPT is about 6 rail slabs more expensive than Mundra for North-bound rail haulage; industry talk of special haulage relief is unconfirmed.
Warehousing market shifting from unorganised to organised; competitive intensity described as ongoing, with CONCOR the largest rail competitor.

qa_highlights.question: Is Gateway's ICD market share holding given the stagnant volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said share is intact and the market itself has de-graded due to the war; double-digit growth for the year is still expected once the situation clears.

qa_highlights.question: How much MAT credit supports the low cash tax rate, and when does full tax apply?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Kartik Aiyer said the company will pay at 18.88% for at least 7-8 years, using accumulated MAT credit; management noted cash tax rose only INR 1-2 crore YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why has rail EBITDA per TEU weakened, and what is the fix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower import share, lower double-stacking, higher underframe and empty running, port imbalance at Mundra and Pipavav, and steep wage hikes (Haryana up 35%); recovery expected as volumes return, with fuel impact visible in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the JNPT exposure and the economics of shifting to it?
qa_highlights.answer: JNPT is about 5% of rail volume; on current pricing it is more expensive for North-bound customers but yields higher revenue and slightly higher EBITDA per TEU for Gateway due to distance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the CFS business and its land?
qa_highlights.answer: A sale was explored about 1.5 years ago without a satisfactory valuation; no active process now, though management is open to a good offer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value of the land bank?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a formal valuation; cited Garhi (85-90 acres) at INR 25-30 crore per acre on outright purchase, with total land of about 475 acres.

risks_watch: Duration of the West Asia conflict and its effect on import volumes and market size.
Port congestion and weather-driven restrictions at Mundra, Pipavav and JNPT affecting double-stacking.
Whether shipping lines actually shift volume to JNPT and whether railways grant JNPT haulage relief.
Rail EBITDA per TEU recovery in Q2 as fuel and wage pass-throughs take effect.
Jaipur ICD litigation outcome (final arguments in September 2026) and Indore/Ankleshwar commissioning timelines.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth but cautious near term: management repeatedly tied the double-digit recovery to the West Asia situation easing and avoided quantifying monthly trends or JNPT shift timing.
key_quotes: So, the market share is intact only. The market has de-grown in the markets that we operate in.
We're looking at growth of, say, 10% to 15% on top line and it will be across all the segments.
We will be paying at the rate of 18.88% for at least 7, 8 years.

adds.what: About 24,000 additional warehousing pallets (Snowman), Pune first then Patna
Ankleshwar ICD EXIM operations start (new EXIM location, one existing ICD about 5,000 TEU)
Indore ICD (land expanded to about 26.4 acres), operational by 2028

growth.why: Management guides 10-15% FY27 top-line growth across all segments (midpoint 12.5%) and Gateway double-digit volume growth, backed by about 24,000 new pallets by end FY27 and Ankleshwar EXIM start in Q2, but tempered by West Asia conflict dependence, weak June-July volumes and rail EBITDA pressure.
